review_rationale: Congress holds enumerated powers to raise and support armies, regulate forces, and appropriate military funding.
scope_limitations: No categorical prohibition on peacetime standing armies; army appropriations are limited to two years.

review_rationale: The Constitution assigns military command to the civilian President.
scope_limitations: Civilian command does not by itself establish all limits on military operations or prove historical causation.

review_rationale: Article VI defines constitutional supremacy and binds federal and state officers by oath or affirmation.
scope_limitations: Supremacy does not independently resolve every jurisdictional dispute or prove a direct response to colonial grievances.

review_rationale: The Third Amendment expressly addresses quartering soldiers, matching the subject of the grievance.
scope_limitations: The Amendment protects houses under specified peacetime and wartime conditions, not every military accommodation.

review_rationale: The Fifth Amendment supplies criminal procedural protections relevant to the integrity of legal proceedings.
scope_limitations: It does not independently require prosecution or punishment of soldiers; structural classification remains provisional pending independent review.
